CGI, like anything else, can be half-assed and/or overused. The movies that are guilty of this are the ones that people criticize. When CGI started to gain popularity, filmmakers had a tendency to be guilty of both overusing CGI and using poorly done CGI (probably in the interest of saving money), so people started to get a bad opinion of it.

Another problem was that the people creating the CGI treated it like traditional animation, making things look cartoony and fake. They're slowly getting away from that school of thought now.

I took computer animation courses at a couple of different schools, and one of the first things that I was taught was how to exaggerate character motion in the way that had traditionally been done with 2d animation. This looks terrible with CGI, because you end up with very realistic models (if they're well done) that have very unrealistic motion, then you have filmmakers trying to mix these cartoon-looking things with live action and it's a big disaster.

Edit: I guess I should have noted that I was talking about CGI when used in live-action films. Pure CGI movies are great, especially when they have a good deal of effort, skill and talent behind their production.

I think the answer we are dancing around is truly right in front of us.

What I mean to say is that the CG in films is great. Giving life and detail to elements in a story that sometimes can't be achieved in practical FX.

There's no clearcut moment for when I started to 'hate' CGI, but I'd have to say in the mid-2000s when it became cheap enough to use CGI for just about every effects shot it started to ruin a lot of 'blockbuster' movies. I like to use Independence Day as an example of why movies were better before CGI became overused. It has puppets and suits for the aliens, which you can see are tangible objects, drawing you into the world. The destruction of the city, which would definitely be made with CGI now, was a scale model and actual fire (whole video is worth watching, by the way). It's a fantastic film which I have watched every year since I was a kid. And, yes, it has CGI in it as well.
CGI can be a very effective tool for filmmakers, but I feel it has become too much of a crutch as of late. There's a reason LotR looks fantastic and The Hobbit looks off. There's a reason action movies don't draw us in anymore.

I do love me some CGI, though. I absolutely love Speed Racer and have had a fondness for Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within since I watched it with my dad when I was a kid. I don't want it to go away, I just want it to be used with more restraint and more wisely.

As for working in the heat, I prefer wearing natural fibers over synthetic. I find that synthetic fibres aren't very breathable and trap a lot of heat.
Thick blinds that won't blow around in the wind attached on the exterior of the house. There's also outdoor shades which might work better.
There's no point in opening south facing windows during the day. If you do it right, it will be hotter inside the house than outside, thus: keep the windows shut.

Whatever passive route you take will be quickly ignored... owl statues, hanging CD's from the tree, bells, whatever. You have to actually kill them.
